title: Chicken Methi Malai
subtitle: A creamy north Indian curry with fenugreek and gentle spice
excerpt: Tender chicken in a pale, cream-based sauce fragrant with dried fenugreek leaves. Mild enough for those who avoid heat, with a distinct herbal note that sets it apart from other cream curries.
sourceNotes: North Indian restaurant tradition, drawing on multiple Anglo-Indian malai curry sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the cream, then stir in fresh cream when reheating. Keeps for up to two months.
recipe.batchNotes: The sauce scales well. Stir the cream in portion by portion at serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the sauce a day ahead and refrigerate. Add cream and reheat gently when ready to serve.

content.text: Methi malai is a north Indian curry where fenugreek leaves and cream do most of the work. Keep the heat low once the cream goes in so it does not split. The sauce should be pale gold and gently coating, not brown.
Heat the oil and butter together in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt. Fry for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 90 seconds. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala. Stir for one minute.
Add the ground almonds if using. Stir through. Add the chicken and stir to coat. Cook for three minutes, turning the pieces so they colour lightly on all sides.
Turn the heat to low. Add the whisked yoghurt, a spoonful at a time, stirring after each addition so it does not split.
Add 120ml of water and the dried fenugreek leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the double cream. Simmer on a very low heat for three minutes. Do not let it boil. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve with naan or rice. The sauce should be lightly coating and pale gold.

items.symptom: The yoghurt has curdled into grainy lumps.
items.cause: It was added too quickly or the pan was too hot.
items.fix: Next time, whisk the yoghurt smooth and add it off the heat in small amounts. If it has curdled, blending the sauce smooth fixes the texture.

items.cause: Too much fenugreek, or the spices were scorched.
items.fix: Start with one tablespoon of fenugreek leaves rather than two. A spoonful of cream and a pinch of sugar can balance bitterness in the finished dish.

items.symptom: The cream has split and looks oily.
items.cause: The heat was too high when the cream was added.
items.fix: Keep the heat very low before stirring in cream. If it splits, remove from heat, add a splash of cold water, and stir vigorously to bring it back.
